newsitem.title: POLAND: Kyungbang buys Polish electronics firm.
newsitem.headline: Kyungbang buys Polish electronics firm.

text.p: South Korea's Kyungbang concern on Wednesday bought 84 percent of the Polish Fonica electronics company for an undisclosed sum and pledged to invest $2.5 million there, a Fonica official said on Thursday.
Lilla Perka, Fonica's legal adviser, told Reuters that Kyungbang would invest $1.5 million by the end of this year.
"The Koreans pledged to invest altogether $2.5 million, with $1.5 million by the end of this year," Perka said.
She said the Korean concern agreed to keep Fonica's 400 jobs for two years and hand over 20 percent of the firm's shares to employees.
The remaining 16 perent of Fonica's stock is in the hands of two cooperative firms, an energy company, a Japanese controlled firm and eight employees.
Fonica was created in 1992 from the Lodz Radio works. It produces electronics, engine parts and toys.
